subject: problematic angle labels in polar plot

messages.author: a3c668b849637905
messages.subject: problematic angle labels in polar plot
parts:
Dear list,

Consider the following code:

library(ggplot2)
d <- data.frame(x=seq(0,2*pi, length.out=100), y=40)
breaksFull <- pi*c(0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, 1, 5/4, 3/2, 7/4)
p <- ggplot(data=d, aes(x,y))+geom_line()+coord_polar()+
scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,2*pi), breaks=breaksFull,
labels=round(breaksFull, 2)) +
scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0, max(d$y)), expand=c(0,0))

ggsave('test.pdf', p, width=4, height=4, units='cm')

There are two issues:

1- the labels are clipped to the plot area

2- I could not manage to push the angle labels (transformed x-axis)
further away from the plot area; the usual vjust/hjust is not
applicable here.

Ideas? Should this be a bug report?

Thanks,

baptiste

The weird thing is that I can't get the vjust to work at all, even without coord_polar(). 

ggplot(data=d,aes(x,y))+
geom_line()+
scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,2*pi),breaks=breaksFull,labels=round(breaksFull, 2))+
scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0, max(d$y)),expand=c(0,0))+
opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(colour="red", vjust=5, hjust = 0))

Can you get around the clipping by increasing the DPI of the output? A 4 cm x 4 cm PDF is kind of an odd size from my perspective.
